items.title: His Ex-Wife Waived His $400,000 Plan in Their Divorce. Her Name on the Beneficiary Form Won in the Supreme Court
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA DuPont employee’s ex-wife collected his savings plan’s balance of about $400,000 when he died in 2001, because her name was still on the beneficiary form even though she had given up those benefits in their divorce. In 2009, a unanimous Supreme Court ruled that the plan was right to pay her, since a workplace plan covered by federal law has to pay by its own documents, and the beneficiary form is one of them.
